Conflict: Material and Design Agent recommends PCR PC/ABS blend for recyclability, while In-Service Agent rejects this due to its lower impact resistance compared to high-impact virgin polycarbonate.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; In-Service Agent
Rationale: PCR PC/ABS is chosen because it significantly reduces the product's carbon footprint and supports circularity through high recyclability. To address the in-service durability concerns, the housing wall thickness and internal ribbing will be optimized rather than relying on non-recyclable glass-fiber reinforcements, satisfying both durability and circularity.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: material durability vs end-of-life recyclability

Conflict: Manufacture Agent recommends integrated snap-fits to minimize assembly energy, while Circularity Agent rejects this because snap-fits are prone to breaking during disassembly, preventing repair and material recovery.
Decision: Standardized metric machine screws with threaded brass inserts
Rationale: Standardized metric machine screws with brass inserts are selected because they enable non-destructive disassembly, which is essential for repairability and high-quality end-of-life recycling. While snap-fits simplify manufacturing, their high failure rate during repair undermines the product's overall lifecycle durability.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: manufacturing simplicity vs repairability and non-destructive disassembly

Conflict: Manufacture Agent recommends a brushed DC motor to avoid the high manufacturing footprint of rare-earth magnets, while In-Service Agent rejects this due to lower efficiency and shorter operating life compared to a brushless motor.
Decision: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with ferrite or recycled magnets
Rationale: A brushless DC motor with ferrite or recycled magnets is selected. This provides the high efficiency and long operational lifespan required for a durable power tool while mitigating the severe environmental impacts associated with mining virgin rare-earth elements.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: manufacturing impact of raw materials vs in-use energy efficiency and durability

Conflict: Manufacture Agent recommends an integrated molded plastic fan for manufacturing simplicity, while Circularity Agent rejects this because active cooling introduces dust and moisture, reducing tool reliability, and prefers a passive aluminum heatsink.
Decision: Passive cooling via recycled aluminum heatsinks
Rationale: Passive cooling via recycled aluminum heatsinks is chosen. It prevents the ingress of abrasive dust and drywall particles into the electronics, thereby extending in-service reliability, and allows for clean, non-destructive material separation at end-of-life.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: active cooling performance vs end-of-life material separation and reliability

Conflict: Manufacture Agent recommends a highly integrated monolithic internal chassis to reduce assembly complexity, while In-Service Agent rejects this because it prevents component-level repair and replacement.
Decision: Modular cartridge system with plug-and-play modules
Rationale: A modular cartridge system is selected because it allows individual worn or failed components (such as the trigger switch or gear module) to be replaced without discarding the entire tool. This significantly extends the product's useful life, representing sustainability best practice.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: manufacturing consolidation vs product repairability and modularity

Conflict: Manufacture Agent recommends an integrated non-removable battery to minimize production waste and material use, while Circularity Agent rejects this because it leads to premature disposal of the entire tool when the battery degrades.
Decision: Removable and standardized slide-on Li-ion battery pack
Rationale: A removable, standardized battery pack is chosen. Because battery cells degrade much faster than the mechanical components of the tool, an integrated battery would lead to premature disposal of the entire screwdriver. A removable pack also ensures safe battery extraction and recycling.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: manufacturing material reduction vs battery replaceability and end-of-life safety
